The analytic cutoff improves from `q < 10^10` to **`q < 50,000,000`**, a factor
of 200, assuming the specified intermediate results of Banks.

This release supplies a self-contained cumulative paper: the original
argument, the new refinement, and the finite classification can all be
read in one document. The original v1 snapshot remains available unchanged.

- [Complete v2 proof](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.2.0/versions/v2/output/pdf/proof.pdf)
- [v2 reproduction files](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/tree/v0.2.0/versions/v2)
- [Mathematical changelog](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.2.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Version-specific review record](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/blob/v0.2.0/versions/v2/REVIEW.md)
- [Original v1 release](https://github.com/twinheterodox/tenth-discriminant/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

The refinement combines `1 - beta < 2/sqrt(q)` with a new application of
Banks's Lemma 4.2, Lemma 5.1, and Corollary 6.3. It gives contradictory
bounds of less than `0.00502` and greater than `0.00509` for
`(1 - beta) log q` when `q >= 50,000,000`.

All 23 exact arithmetic checks pass. The original sieve programs and
recorded outputs are reused byte-for-byte; their larger range covers the
entire remaining interval. The final nine-discriminant list is unchanged.

**The new refinement has not yet received a separate-model mathematical
cross-check.** The reported v1 cross-check applies only to the original
argument. Banks's intermediate results remain external inputs, and no
Lean formalization is supplied.

This is an AI-assisted research draft, published as a prerelease for review.
